title: GORE-TEX Brand blog — 2-layer, 2.5-layer and 3-layer waterproof construction
claims: Waterproof-breathable garments come in 2-layer, 2.5-layer and 3-layer constructions: the face fabric sits outside, the membrane is the waterproof-breathable middle layer, and the inner layer protects the membrane from sweat and oil that could clog its pores.

A 3-layer garment uses a durable PU/backer laminated directly to the membrane; a 2.5-layer garment uses a very thin, painted-on half layer; a 2-layer garment typically uses a hanging mesh liner that is less effective and less lightweight.

3-layer garments are more durable but pricier, while 2.5-layer is lighter and more packable; a DWR chemical treatment on the face fabric keeps it from absorbing water without inhibiting membrane breathability.
During high-intensity uphill activity, sweat-soaked clothing can lead to hypothermia, which is why pant breathability matters; lower-intensity standing activity can accept a heavier 2-layer garment.
